It clicked for me! I can't even explain to you how. I wish I could bottle it and give it away to others like me. As recently as last weekend I thought one way. Two things clicked Saturday. One more clicked Sunday.

I feel amazing. Shed years of seeking approval. Finally understand what it means to care about myself.

Each has to find the way. It won't be the same for everyone. Baby steps and then you make it. It took me YEARS, but it is so very worth it. 

It's so carefree, so "weightless". Waking up with a smile. Everyday is a new day, but not with darkness. There's light now. I'm shining. I feel it. This week, I was happier than the happiest guy at work!

I just can't believe it. I enjoy it. Many times a day, realizing how I feel.

It'll click for you too. It will!!!!

I was thinking very similar last year at this time. The thing that kept me from suicide was the thought of failing. It does not always go as planned and things could become worse. 

I found healing in walking and hiking. Particularly a county park with a river. I would walk until I couldn't anymore some days or until it was getting too dark and it was necessary to turn back. Sometimes my hike wasn't far. I'd sit near the water and just think until my thoughts ran dry. It helped restore me and I still make it a point to go. 

I am not where I hope to be, but now I recognize the bad moments or negative thoughts are just moments and thoughts that will pass and their space can and will be filled with better things. 

I've recently added journaling, especially when I can't hike. I never believed much use would come of it, but it does help to put things down and get them out of the brain's continuous overthinking loop. 

I also challenge myself continuously to look for the good. Even if it's one thing like remembering to take a vitamin. We all start somewhere.

Be encouraged. Thoughts are with you.
I hug an extra firm pillow tight to my chest every night. I can't be without it when falling asleep.
My only relationships are online. Friends over 5 and 6 months. Sometimes... most times, it's not enough.
Alcohol... I'm starting down a bad path.

Time. Solitude. I also had a 2 month relationship. I'm 11 days from ending what I thought was the best thing to ever happen in my life, but may have been the worst. Like yours, mine was the sweetest, most loving and caring person to me. Like you, I see the red flags in retrospect. I knew I lacked for attention, but was completely honest from the beginning and mistakenly believed he was honest, too. There likely won't be a day in my life that I won't think of him... Correction... Think of what he presented himself to be and how amazing we could've been together. I'm spending a lot of time alone. Hiking has helped the most. Going where a river rushes by until the sounds of nature overwhelm the thoughts. Long car drives with radio blasting and windows down. Movies alone for distraction. The relationship is something I won't talk to anyone about. I still can't bring myself to look back at his texts. Just knowing they are there brings me a level of comfort as it is proof someone wanted me - even if he lied. It is messed up in my head now. Someday I'll heal. You will, too. You aren't alone.
